subject: Residency variant rollout — EU primary + APAC warm-standby (SLA & SOW negotiation)
messages:
From: Emma Liao <emma.liao@cardiomed.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@cardiomed.com>, procurement@cardiomed.com
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Residency options for renewal — follow up

Hi Marcus,

Thanks for the call this morning. A few follow-ups from our side: cardiology apps must have primary residency in the EU for regulatory reasons, but we would like an APAC warm-standby for traffic surges and regional latency during APAC business hours.

Key asks from procurement/eng:
- Confirm whether Redwood can offer EU-primary tenancy with an APAC warm-standby failover and what the SLA looks like for cross-region failover (RTO/RPO expectations).
- Pricing uplift for reserved capacity in EU + standby nodes in APAC (we plan to scale from 50 TPS to 150 TPS during peak campaigns).
- An outline of the cutover and failover test plan during renewal window.

Procurement would like a redlined SOW and an SLA matrix by next Wednesday (12/2) to push to their security and legal teams.

Best,
Emma
Head of Cloud Ops, CardioMed Systems

-----Original Message-----
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Emma Liao <emma.liao@cardiomed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Residency options for renewal — follow up

Emma — thanks for the clear list. We can support the EU-primary + APAC warm-standby pattern. High-level responses below; I will follow up with a formal SOW + SLA matrix.

- Architecture: EU primary (isolated tenancy per your request) with APAC warm-standby nodes that accept cold traffic and can be promoted during failover. Traffic routing via our smart router with health checks and automatic promotion.
- SLA: For primary-region requests we offer 99.95% availability (per contract). For planned cross-region failover, we can commit to a documented failover runbook and a target RTO of 30 minutes for session-level continuity, with awareness that cold-cache promotion may add latency for the first N tokens. RPO is near-zero for persisted customer data since we replicate logs/metrics asynchronously to EU primary and archive to encrypted storage; we'll include specifics in the SLA matrix.
- Pricing: We propose a reserved-capacity uplift for EU primary (committed vGPU pool) and a smaller warm-standby pool in APAC billed as standby capacity plus a small per-token failover premium. I will propose pricing tiers in the SOW.

Marissa / Ben / Neha — can you confirm the following by Monday?
1) Sizing assumptions for EU dedicated vGPU pool and APAC standby (I put a first-pass guess: EU 8xA100 equiv for steady 50 TPS, burst to 150 TPS with autoscale to 20 nodes; APAC warm-standby 4xA100 equiv as standby).
2) Whether we can include a 2-week staged failover test during the renewal month (customer expects this as part of acceptance).
3) Any recommended language for the RTO/RPO sections and the failback guarantee.

Thanks — I will attach the draft SOW and SLA matrix by EOD Mon.

— Marcus
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

-----Original Message-----
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Residency options for renewal — follow up

Folks — quick notes on sizing and commercial posture.

1) Sizing: I agree with Marcus's baseline. For CardioMed we should plan for 25% headroom on all proposals during year 1. So EU steady-state = 10 nodes (reserve), burst autoscale to 25 nodes. APAC warm-standby = 5 standby nodes. I will update the capacity_worksheet attached.
2) Commercial: Recommend a 12-month renewal with a 10% uplift to list for the reserved capacity, and include a 60-day early-exit clause if CardioMed doesn't hit usage thresholds. For the APAC standby, price as 'standby reservation' at 40% of full reserved price plus per-token failover usage.
3) Tests: Include a staged failover runbook with a canary cutover in week 2 after deployment and a full failover test in week 6. Scope the test so we don't take production offline — use mirrored traffic for the canary.

CC: Ben, Neha — need legal-approved SLA language and an ops-runbook template we can hand to Emma.

Marissa
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

-----Original Message-----
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:10:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Residency options for renewal — follow up

Agree on the sizing and commercial framing. A couple of technical caveats to include in the SOW/SLA:
- Cold-cache promotion: first-request latency during failover may be up to 2-3x normal until KV caches warm; call this out explicitly and include mitigation (prefix caching + warmed replicas for critical models).
- Data replication: we need to be clear about what 'near-zero' RPO means — we replicate inference logs and telemetry continuously, but if they need cross-region synchronous state for other systems (e.g., billing events), we'll need to scope it separately.

I'll draft the ops-runbook appendix (cutover checklist, rollback criteria, test cases).

Ben
Director, Platform Reliability, Redwood Inference

-----Original Message-----
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Emma Liao <emma.liao@cardiomed.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:38:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Residency variant rollout — draft SOW attached

Emma — attaching the draft SOW and SLA matrix for your review (see links / attachments). Highlights:
- Term: 12 months (auto-renew), with an optional 6-month canary extension at a fee-discount for staged APAC activation.
- Capacity: Reserved EU pool sized at 10 nodes (baseline) with autoscale to 25 for campaign windows. APAC warm-standby reserved at 5 nodes; standby billing at 40% of reserved list plus per-token charge during failover.
- Failover SLA: Targeted RTO 30 minutes for routing cutover; note cold-cache latency delta called out. Rollback criteria and acceptance tests included.
- Security/compliance: EU residency guaranteed; audit logs and KMS keys remain under CardioMed's control for the EU tenancy.

Next steps: please confirm signoff items by COB Wednesday (2026-12-02) if you'd like procurement/legal to proceed. If desired, we can schedule a 30-min walk-through on Thursday to review redlines.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Renewals Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_SOW_v3_Cardiomed.pdf (SOW draft), SLA_vs_Tiers_2026-11.xlsx (matrix), Capacity_worksheet_Cardiomed.csv (sizing)

-----Original Message-----
From: Emma Liao <emma.liao@cardiomed.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2026 07:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Residency variant rollout — draft SOW attached

Neha — thank you, this is helpful. A couple of procurement redlines:
1) Add a 45-day remediation SLA for any data residency misconfiguration (CardioMed requires clear penalties for residency breaches).
2) Can you expand the acceptance test to explicitly include 1) mirrored traffic canary and 2) a documented failback timebox?
3) We want a DocuSign link for the SOW; procurement will route the SLA to legal after SOW signoff.

If you can accept those changes we'll route to legal on Thursday. Otherwise, let's schedule the 30-min review.

Emma
Head of Cloud Ops, CardioMed Systems

-----Original Message-----
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Emma Liao <emma.liao@cardiomed.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2026 14:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Residency variant rollout — draft SOW attached

Emma — appreciate the clear redlines. We can:
- Add the 45-day remediation SLA clause for residency misconfigurations (with mutually agreed remediation steps and at-specified credits).
- Expand acceptance tests to include the mirrored-traffic canary and a 2-hour documented failback target in normal operations (failback timeboxed; we will include timing caveats if region-wide incidents are the root cause).

I'll push an updated SOW + DocuSign link by EOD. Marissa — please prepare the commercial summary for the DocuSign package (pricing tiers, early-exit clause, canary extension). Ben/Neha — finalize the ops-runbook appendix.

Next meeting: propose Thu 12/3 09:00 PT to walk procurement/legal through the SOW. Emma — does that time work?

— Marcus
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
